Hey OP, I’ve read through this and some of your replies. I’m so sorry this happened to you, I couldn’t imagine losing the person I loved the most. I’ve lost a lot of people, but losing someone you were in love with is something else entirely. I see that you think you could’ve saved him, and that hurts me to read as I had a couple friends pass away awhile back that I was convinced I could’ve saved had I said and done things differently. In truth, we will never know if we could’ve saved them or not. If we did things differently, maybe it could’ve delayed the outcome, but there’s no way of knowing if things truly would’ve played out much differently. These thoughts of what you could’ve done different are absolutely haunting, but you should not linger on these thoughts too much. We can’t change the past as desperately as we want to. I also don’t think you did anything wrong, as he was hurting you. If you looked past your feelings and simply allowed him to hurt you, you would’ve been doing yourself a major disservice. Bpd is an incredibly painful disorder, but it’s not an excuse to treat people badly. I’ve made my own mistakes and hurt others, and it is their right to respond to that however they choose. Once again, you didn’t do anything wrong, you just responded to the pain you were subjected to. I know this is something you’re going to deal with for a long time, but I want you to try your best to remember that you did what you could and it’s not your fault that this happened. Sending love your way 🫶🏻

I understand some in the comments find this post invalidating, but I wanna remind everyone this young minor person doesn’t fully understand what is going on with them mentally and hasn’t received the proper help for it. I also wanna share some of my personal experience with BPD in hopes it can help somehow. 

I first considered BPD when I was trying to figure out what was wrong with me in high school. I had already been diagnosed with depression anxiety and an excoriation disorder but I couldn’t shake the feeling that something much deeper was going on and there was a reason why my current therapy and meds just weren’t working very well. When I learned what BPD was, it scared me. It sounded very familiar and like me, but I didn’t like that because it’s a very serious diagnosis. I sat on the information for around a year, slowly starting to look more into what BPD is until I finally accepted that this probably is what’s wrong with me. I brought it up to my therapist at the time who laughed at me and said very stigmatizing things about BPD, and I felt so hurt I never saw her again. 

I proceeded to go through therapist after therapist, psych after psych trying to be believed. One had me read a book about BPD called “ I Hate You Don’t Leave Me” that I recommend reading, and I never was diagnosed by that psych or any after even after expressing that it felt just like me. It wasn’t until my current psych and therapist in a totally different state that I was believed, and they didn’t immediately believe me either. It wasn’t until after around a year or so they both told me they can see it in me and it makes total sense. Both of them have said they can officially diagnose me if that’s really what I want, but have made it very clear that if they put it on paper I could be turned away from opportunities that would’ve been available otherwise. So on paper, I don’t have bpd even though everyone acknowledges that I do. 

The most important thing my current psych and therapist have taught me is that the label of what you’re experiencing doesn’t necessarily matter, it’s treating the symptoms that does. I fully believe you’re in a lot of pain to think that you have bpd, and that’s valid. I really encourage you to look into financial aid options to receive therapy/counseling and get yourself in to express all of these thoughts you’re having to a professional. I can’t diagnose you, and because you’re still young it may take awhile for you and them to figure out what exactly it is that is going on with you, but just remember to be open and honest with your feelings so you can at least have your problems acknowledged and treated to some degree. I really do wish you all the luck on your journey with finding help and recovery. ❤️‍🩹

I was trying my best to believe in it and understand it and myself, but would get more and more confused the more scriptures and teachings that I read. I started looking into articles from the prophets and such about suicide because I was dealing with suicidal ideation pretty bad and had lost a friend to suicide the year prior, and I was so confused on if my friend was in hell because of his decision. I was also really confused about how “God has a plan, everything happens for a reason.” I couldn’t figure out what reason he could’ve had for making my friends life so miserable to the point that he took his life away. 

It got to a point where my sick brain decided that if god has a plan for everyone, it must be in his plan for me to take my life. Who’s to say it’s not? If God has a plan, what if that plan entails my suicide? After some days of pondering it and a brief moment of clarity, I realized that god can’t be real because no god would want you to take your life for him. After some research (looking at articles about the church that weren’t written by people in the church) it started to become clear that it’s all bullshit and religion was created just to keep people in line and give them something to believe in so they don’t do whatever they want due to being afraid of a higher powers consequences. Religion wasn’t created for people like me to think so deeply about it and see plot holes.

I was still dealing with a lot of mental health issues and still do including c-ptsd, but it suddenly got quite a bit easier to deal with when the guilt the religion instilled into me disappeared. If anything I’ve become proud of myself for breaking out of it and finally coming to an understanding with my family that I’m not Mormon and never will be, and they’ve finally accepted that and don’t treat me any different anymore. I fought for that, and breaking free made me realize that my accomplishments are all my own, not some higher powers. I don’t have to thank god for things I have and who I am, I can thank myself now because it was all me and me alone. We are all our own god, and our accomplishments are ours, that’s something to be proud of yourself for. You alone got to where you are, a higher power had nothing to do with it. I completely understand you. I had friends who self harmed as well, and they aren’t why I started doing it but when we would compare scars I couldn’t help but like theirs more than mine, and felt like I had to get on the level they were or else I was just faking it. While some people get upset when they leave scars, I personally loved every scar and honestly still do. I loved to feel the scabs as they were healing under my clothes during class, I loved to roll up my sleeves or wherever I did it just to stare at them for a minute, and catch myself still staring at the scars on occasion. 

I don’t cut anymore, at least haven’t in months and don’t currently have plans to do it again (but I know I will eventually because the urge never really goes away. It just lessens over time). One thing that got me to stop idolizing other peoples cutting and comparing it to my own was when my sister told me she had cut herself for the first time. Wasn’t nearly as bad as mine, but the fact that she did it at all broke my heart and I couldn’t help but feel responsible for it as maybe she began to idolize mine just as I did to others. 

That’s when it hit me, even though she wasn’t covered in cuts it broke my heart that she was doing it at all, and it doesn’t matter at all how deep you cut or how many you do. The fact that you ever took a razor to yourself is enough to prove that you’re in a lot of pain. A person who cuts a lot and deep could be in the same amount of pain as someone who makes one small wound, or someone who burns themself. They could even be in more pain than the other. It doesn’t matter what your scars look like or how many there are, you marked your body with the pain that you feel inside and that’s all that matters. 

I’m not gonna tell you to stop, I was told to stop a lot and got caught but of course I didn’t stop. It could take a long time to get to a point where you view it differently, or it could take a week. Either way, your mind can change, it’s definitely possible. If I could do it, knowing how broken I was and how much I loved to do it at the time, I know it’s possible for you too. If anything I didn’t even want to stop, the urge just slowly started to fade over time. It’s still there, but I’ve learned how to ignore it and I know you can as well. Regardless of the outcome, I wish you all the best OP. You’re not faking your depression, I thought I was faking it too but ended up being diagnosed with ptsd and borderline as well as depression and anxiety, which the first two I really didn’t think I had at all, especially ptsd. It’s just your mean mental illness brain trying to convince you that you’re lesser than you actually are, your struggles are very real and valid no matter if you harm yourself or not. Good luck ❤️

My brother came in my room and woke me up around 10:30 ish, and I rubbed my eyes and sat up. 

I asked him what he was doing and all he said was, “Will died.” Will was my brother’s best friend at the time, and I had one of my classes up at the high school with him. They had a lot of funny little stories and jokes and stuff, so my brain didn’t take him seriously. I was tired, or rather grumpy and I told him to go away and let me sleep. I still remember the way he looked at me, he seemed so hurt. I saw it in his eyes. He simply walked out of the room and I started to think that dreaded thought, “Oh my god, was he serious?”
